name: PT Indomobil Sukses Internasional Tbk

frontmatter.title: Indomobil: a price that already pays for the pre-revaluation assets
frontmatter.summary: Indomobil trades at the pre-revaluation value of what it owns, not below it. The listed Indomobil Multi Jasa stake is marked at market and the distribution, assembly, industrial and property book at book equity before the PSAK 16 revaluation surplus; after a wide holdco discount the parts are worth less than the price. Operating cash flow is negative and the balance sheet is short-funded. We initiate at SELL.
thesis: On its parts the group is worth less than the price: the listed majority stake is marked at market, the remaining distribution, assembly and industrial book at pre-revaluation equity, and a wide holdco discount is applied. The PSAK 16 revaluation surplus is an appraisal mark, not cash or a realisable amount, so it is not in the base [S5][S3].

Operating cash flow has broken: an outflow in the nine months to September 2026, short-term financial liabilities an order of magnitude above cash, and an interest bill that consumes almost all of operating income on the audited year [S3][S5].

Earnings quality: FY2025 profit carries a large one-off bargain-purchase gain, and parent earnings on a true last-twelve-month basis are negative, so the earnings multiple cannot carry a valuation and we do not weight it [S5][S3].
Tax: the LK pays the statutory rate on operating profit; the much higher levered effective rate is parent-level permanent differences and must not be applied to EBIT [S5].
Governance keeps the discount wide: concentrated control, a thin float, related-party purchases at a fifth of cost of revenue, and a discounted raise as the likeliest recapitalisation route [S8][S3].

catalysts.event: Full-year Gaikindo wholesales and the group December volume report; the industry target is the first test of whether revenue growth is share gain or market recovery [S6].
FY2026 audited accounts: refinancing of the short-term loan book, any going-concern emphasis, and the first full year of the INA consolidation [S3][S9].
Annual general meeting and the dividend decision; the parent payout is the only cash return the minority controls [S8].

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of Indomobil Sukses Internasional with a SELL rating and a target price of Rp458, which is -38.5% from the Rp745 price. The company is the largest listed automotive distributor in Indonesia and the holding vehicle for a listed consumer-finance and rental group, a distribution and assembly business, and an industrial and property portfolio [S5][S3]. The equity trades at a small fraction of reported book, but that book is inflated by a revaluation surplus that the price already pays for; measured against the parts before the mark, there is no gap, and that is the investment case.

The operating story is weak and we do not pretend otherwise. Revenue in the nine months to September 2026 grew by a fifth against the prior year, yet gross margin fell by more than a point and a half and operating income was lower than a year earlier, because vehicle discounting and imported-unit costs consumed the gain [S3]. Finance charges of 2,585.5 against operating income of 2,820.5 leave cover near one time, and the nine-month figures show the same arithmetic [S5][S3]. A business that earns its interest bill and little else does not compound, and its free cash flow stays negative through most of our forecast [S5].

The balance sheet has stopped self-funding. Operating cash flow was an outflow of several trillion rupiah in the nine months to September 2026 against an inflow a year earlier, cash fell, and short-term loans rose [S3]. Financial liabilities falling due within a year are an order of magnitude larger than the cash balance, so the group depends on rolling short-term bank lines and on the bond windows of its multi-finance subsidiaries [S3]. That is the risk that justifies a wide discount, and it is why the target is a value for the parts rather than a cash-flow forecast [S3][S5].

What the company owns is real but already in the price. The value is built from two blocks: the controlling stake in listed PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk, marked at the market price of the subsidiary shares, and the non-IMJ distribution, assembly, industrial and property businesses, carried at the book equity attributable to Indomobil before the PSAK 16 revaluation surplus [S5][S3]. We deduct a holdco discount at the wide end of the house band because control is concentrated, the float is thin and related-party flows are large [S8][S3]. The gross sum of the parts, before any discount, is the mark the price should be measured against, and the price sits 7% below it; after the holdco discount the parts are worth Rp479 a share, below the price [S0][S3].

The catalyst is not a car-market recovery, and none is needed for the rating. It would take a capital-structure or corporate event that makes the asset value reachable by minorities at more than the pre-revaluation book: a disposal of industrial or property assets at the appraised value, a term extension of the short book, a dividend upstream from the listed subsidiary, or a transaction that narrows the discount [S3][S8]. Absent one of those, the equity is priced at its pre-revaluation assets while the cash flow is fragile [S5][S3].

Indomobil is a holding company whose consolidated revenue comes from four activities: vehicle distribution and after-sales, consumer financing and leasing, vehicle rental and logistics, and a residual group of industrial, property and service businesses. The automotive segment earns the overwhelming majority of revenue but, after the allocation of finance income and finance charges, recorded a net loss in FY2025 while the smaller financial-services and other segments carried the consolidated profit [S5]. That allocation is the single most important fact about the group: the distribution business is loss-making at the net level even before the parent interest bill [S5].

The "Others" segment is the profit centre the draft under-described. It earned IDR1,892.8bn of net income in FY2025 on a much smaller revenue base, and it holds the industrial and property assets [S5]. Part of that result is non-recurring: the group booked bargain-purchase gains on the INA, RMM and ISJ acquisitions inside other operating income [S5]. We therefore do not capitalise the segment FY2025 earnings; we carry its assets at pre-revaluation book equity in the sum of the parts [S3][S5].

The distribution business holds Indonesian franchises for several Japanese and European brands and sells through a dealer network that the group partly owns and partly franchises, supported by workshops, spare-parts warehousing and body-and-paint operations [S5][S10]. The consumer-finance arm lends to buyers of the group and third-party vehicles and is funded by bank loans and publicly issued bonds; the rental and logistics arm owns a fleet it leases to corporates [S5]. The group completed the acquisition of Nissan Motor Indonesia through its National Assemblers subsidiary, which brings assembly capacity in addition to distribution [S9].

The group is also a battery-electric participant, not only a victim of the transition. It owns a majority of Aion Indomobil Distribution Indonesia and the whole of Indomobil Zeeda Energi, and it acquired 99.9% of INA (formerly NMI) for a purchase price that generated the bargain gain [S5]. Those businesses sit inside the consolidated automotive and other segments, so their earnings are inside the book equity we value; they are not separately marked, and we say so rather than assigning them zero [S5]. The residual risk is that the BEV channel earns a lower margin than the legacy franchise, which is why we do not add a separate growth value for it [S7].
The group employs 8,294 people across distribution, workshops and the finance and rental businesses, a fixed-cost base that does not flex with volume [S0].

Indomobil is one of the oldest automotive groups in Indonesia, built from a trading house into a distributor, assembler and financier. Its economics are those of a distributor with a captive finance arm: distribution earns a thin gross margin on a large revenue base and needs working capital for inventory, while the finance arm earns a spread on a loan book funded with matched borrowings. The holding company sits above both and services the debt that funded the build-out, which is why consolidated profit is far more sensitive to the interest rate and the funding mix than to the number of cars sold.

Control is concentrated. Gallant Venture, the Salim group Singapore-listed investment holding company, holds 49.5% of the shares as of the end of May 2026, with the Thohir family securities house and a second strategic holder accounting for most of the remainder [S8]. The free float reported by the IDX registry is 7.3% of the shares [S0]. The secondary register we hold is internally inconsistent, its holder lines summing above one hundred percent, so we use the exchange figure and do not build a register-based float argument [S8][S0].

The Indonesian car market is a volume market with a policy-driven cost structure. Wholesales reached 679,020 units in the nine months to September 2026, and the industry association targets a full year that requires a strong fourth quarter [S6]. Battery-electric vehicles took 15.9% of the total market in the first half of 2026, a share that has moved from negligible to material within a few years [S7].

For an incumbent distributor the electric transition is a margin problem before it is a volume problem. The group franchise portfolio is weighted toward Japanese internal-combustion models, which carry the workshop and spare-parts annuity that funds the dealer network; a battery-electric fleet needs less scheduled maintenance and is sold by competitors who do not carry the legacy cost base [S7][S10]. The group response has been to add agency and distribution agreements, including the Aion channel and the INA assembly acquisition, rather than to build its own brand [S9][S5].

The competitive position is strong in absolute scale and weak in relative growth. Indomobil is among the largest distributors in the country, with multi-brand coverage and a national workshop footprint, but the addressable market is shifting toward entrants that do not need its dealer network [S6][S7]. The moat is the franchise relationship and the workshop estate, both contractual or physical rather than structural, and both replicable by a well-capitalised entrant with a factory behind it.

Competition has shifted from brand against brand to channel against channel. Chinese manufacturers are appointing new distributors and building their own networks rather than using the incumbents, so the share they take is lost to the existing dealer estate rather than recirculated through it [S7]. Indomobil defence is to be the partner of choice for whichever brand needs a national footprint, which is what the assembly acquisition and the additional agency agreements amount to [S9]. That defence protects revenue but not margin, because a new brand wants a low price to build share while the distributor carries the showroom and workshop cost [S7].

The Indonesian car market is a cyclical volume market driven by household credit, the rupiah and the policy treatment of luxury goods. Distributors earn a gross margin on the vehicle, a second margin on financing arranged through a captive or partner finance company, and a third, higher-margin annuity on parts and labour over the life of the car. That third leg is why the dealer network has value beyond the showroom, and it is the leg that a battery-electric fleet erodes. Industry practice is to fund inventory with short-term bank lines and the loan book with bonds and medium-term bank debt, which makes the whole chain sensitive to the funding market rather than only to the sales market.

The regulatory regime matters twice: final income tax on vehicle sales is levied on turnover, so it is a fixed cost per unit irrespective of profitability, and the luxury-goods tax and down-payment rules move demand between quarters [S5][S6]. Both are outside management control and both explain why the group levered effective tax charge is far above the statutory rate even though operating profit is taxed at the standard rate [S5].

Revenue has compounded at a low single-digit rate over the five years to FY2025 and then accelerated in the nine months to September 2026, when the group reported 30,505.5 for the prior full year and a nine-month figure well above the comparable period [S5][S3]. The acceleration is not translating into profit: gross margin fell from the FY2025 audited level, operating income for the nine months was below the prior-year comparable, and the parent share of net profit collapsed to a negligible figure [S3]. Minority interests absorbed a larger share of a smaller profit because the profitable finance and rental subsidiaries are partly owned while the loss-making distribution arm is wholly owned [S5].

The cost structure is dominated by two items the equity holder cannot influence. Finance charges of 2,585.5 are set by the debt stock and the rate, and depreciation of 1,351.4 is set by the asset base; together they exceed operating income [S5]. The group final tax on turnover adds a further charge that rises as a proportion of profit when profit falls, which is why the levered effective rate on the audited year was far above the statutory rate [S5].

We restate the accounts where the data pack or the draft was wrong. Depreciation is restated to the audited total, roughly three times the pack figure, and operating income to the reported line [S5]. Dividends paid are restated to the amount paid to parent shareholders, because the pack includes the large distribution to non-controlling interests that never touches parent equity [S5][S8]. Tax is charged at the statutory rate disclosed in the notes, not at the levered effective rate: the excess over statutory is a parent-level non-deductible item plus final-taxed dividend and rent income, none of which scales with consolidated EBIT [S5]. Operating expenses are calibrated on the nine months to September 2026, which are clean of the bargain-purchase gains, so the forecast does not embed non-recurring other operating income [S3][S5].

Cash generation is the central operating problem. Capital expenditure of 2,890.2 exceeded operating cash flow of IDR2,040.2bn in the audited year, and the nine months to September 2026 produced a large operating outflow as the financing book and inventory absorbed cash [S5][S3]. Our forecast carries capital expenditure converging from the expansion rate toward depreciation plus growth, working capital at the observed level to revenue, and net new borrowing that funds the gap, which is what the group has actually done [S3][S5]. On that arithmetic free cash flow to the firm is IDR-2,951.3bn in FY2026E and turns positive only in the final years of the forecast, reaching IDR2,777.1bn in FY2035E [S5].

Debt is short and large. Financial liabilities falling due within a year are an order of magnitude above the cash balance, and the group discloses little committed undrawn capacity against them [S3]. The multi-finance subsidiaries issue bonds to match the loan book, but the parent-level working-capital lines roll quarterly, so a funding-market closure transmits directly into a liquidity event rather than into a margin problem [S3][S5]. The forecast balance sheet rolls from the audited December 2025 position through the cash flow and therefore sits below what the group has already reported: net debt at 30 September 2026 already stood above the model's FY2026E line [S3], and the engine's cash line is a balancing item, so the FY2026E net-debt line understates the interim. We disclose the gap rather than forecast the reversal, and the valuation does not depend on it because the parts are balance-sheet marks taken from the September interim [S3].

Earnings quality is assessed on the right tests for a group with a finance book. We do not use the Sloan accruals ratio, which is meaningless on a financial balance sheet; the relevant test is provisioning against write-offs on the financing receivables, where the policy writes off receivables overdue more than six months and provisions are assessed individually and collectively under the expected-credit-loss model [S5]. The fixed-asset revaluation surplus of IDR6,847.1bn is more than half of parent equity, and a further IDR3,240.0bn of investment-property fair-value gain sits in retained earnings because the group took it through profit or loss rather than through a revaluation reserve, so the book value is a mark rather than a cost [S5][S3]. Related-party purchases were IDR4,902.6bn in the nine months to September 2026, about a fifth of cost of revenue, and other receivables from related parties were IDR3,220.2bn, a claim on affiliates equal to a material share of parent equity [S3].

We value Indomobil as a holding company on its parts, which is the house method for a group whose equity is a claim on a listed subsidiary plus a portfolio of operating and property assets [S5][S3]. The cost of equity is built from a risk-free rate of 7.4%, a mature-market equity risk premium, a country risk premium and a levered beta of 2.30 obtained by relevering the industry asset beta at the group market gearing of 2.00 times [S5]. The gearing is the engine two-times cap applied to a market debt-to-equity ratio of roughly nineteen times, so the cost of equity of 21.2% is high because the equity is a thin stub, not because of an arbitrary input [S0][S5]. It is used only to roll the fundamental value forward twelve months, not to discount operating cash flow.

The sum of the parts has two blocks. The first is the controlling stake in listed PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk, marked at the market price of the subsidiary shares, which values the 49.5% holding well below its attributable book equity [S5]. That mark is deliberate, because the listed shares trade at a fraction of book and a holding company should not capitalise its own carrying value [S5]. The second is the non-IMJ distribution, assembly, industrial and property businesses, carried at the book equity attributable to Indomobil on the September 2026 interim balance sheet, net of the IMJ stake, of the non-controlling interests and of the PSAK 16 revaluation surplus [S3]. The gross sum of the parts, before any holdco discount, is the mark the price should be measured against, and the price sits 7% below it.

The revaluation surplus we exclude is the fixed-asset mark: IDR6,847.1bn at FY2025A plus the land movement in the nine months [S5][S3]. It is an appraisal reserve, not a cash flow, and no source supports an acquirer paying it at face, so EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS requires the pre-revaluation basis and the base mark uses it [S5][S3]. What the pre-revaluation book still includes is the IDR3,240.0bn investment-property fair-value gain, because the group recognised it through profit or loss and it now sits in retained earnings rather than in a revaluation reserve; the base therefore strips the fixed-asset mark and not that gain [S3]. The investments in shares sit inside the book at carrying value and are therefore not valued at zero [S5]. They are IDR4,300.4bn in total, split between associates at equity-method carrying value and a fair-valued portfolio, and the associates named in the note are Hino Motors Sales Indonesia, Hino Finance Indonesia, Furukawa Indomobil Battery Manufacturing, Kyokuto Indomobil Manufacturing Indonesia and the Inchcape Indomobil distribution and manufacturing entities, none of which is a listed Tbk, so there is no market mark to use and the carrying value is the sourced mark we carry [S3]. The IMJ subtraction uses the subsidiary book equity from the 30 June 2026 data pack because the interim accounts do not restate it at 30 September; the one-quarter mismatch is disclosed rather than estimated [S0][S3].

We apply a holdco discount of 40%, at the wide end of the house band, and then the house liquidity ladder takes a further twenty percent because the stock trades below the minimum turnover threshold [S8][S3]. The discount is the base rate for holding companies, not an opportunity: it persists indefinitely unless a dated catalyst narrows it [S8]. The governance file justifies the wide end: concentrated control, a thin float, related-party purchases at a fifth of cost of revenue, a large claim on affiliates, and an equity base half of which is an appraisal mark [S8][S3][S5]. The name's own record supports the wide end: its reported price to book was 0.2x at the FY2025A accounts and has never approached book in the audited years, so the market has never paid anything close to the parts, and there is no five-year episode of a narrow discount to point to [S0]. The house base rate for discount narrowing completes only a third of the time over three years, with a wide outcome spread, so we do not assume it narrows [S8].

The consolidated discounted cash flow is shown as a cross-check, not as a weighted method. Free cash flow to the firm is negative through the middle of the forecast because capital expenditure, tax at the statutory rate and the working-capital absorption of the finance book exceed operating profit; a perpetuity cannot rescue a stream that is negative for most of its life, and the enterprise value therefore falls below net debt and floors at zero [S5][S3]. We do not pretend that a floored method is a valuation: weighting it would put most of the target on a zero, which is exactly the error the red team identified in the prior draft [S3].

The earnings multiple is not available on a defensible base. Parent earnings on a true last-twelve-month basis are negative once the fourth quarter of FY2025 is included, and the FY2025 figure that the prior draft used is inflated by the "Others" segment result and by the bargain-purchase gains [S3][S5]. Applying a multiple to a negative or one-off-inflated base would produce a number without meaning, so we do not weight it; the normalised earnings path in the financial summary is the operating check the reader should watch [S3].

The sensitivity that matters is the discount, not the discount rate. The parts are a balance-sheet mark, so a change in the cost of equity moves only the twelve-month roll-forward, while a ten-point change in the holdco discount moves the target by more than a quarter [S8][S3]. That is why the scenarios are built on the discount and why the signposts in the next section are corporate events rather than volume beats [S8].

The reverse arithmetic is the clearest statement of the gap. The price sits only 7% below the gross pre-revaluation sum of the parts, so the market is already paying the full pre-revaluation asset value before any holding-company discount; to reach our value the parts have to be discounted for control, related-party leakage and illiquidity, which is what the house framework does and the market does not [S3][S5]. We read the price as an asset value that assumes the pre-revaluation book is worth its face, and the investment case as the absence of any cushion if it is not.

The downside case is a governance and funding discount rather than a demand event. If the multi-finance book stops growing and consumer-finance defaults rise, the group loses the profit centre that carries the consolidated result while the interest bill on the short-term loan book is unchanged [S3][S5]. Because financial liabilities due within a year dwarf cash, a refusal by banks to roll the lines would force asset sales at the worst point in the cycle, and the revaluation surplus in equity would not help because it is not cash [S3][S5].

A discounted equity raise is a downside, not a remedy. At a fraction of book, with control at 49.5% and a float of 7.3%, the cheapest recapitalisation for the controller is a placement or rights issue at a discount, which transfers value from minorities to the subscriber [S8][S3]. We carry that in the bear case as a wider discount rather than as a share-count change, because the size and price of any raise are not disclosed; the dilution arithmetic is simply that a raise below the pre-raise price reduces per-share value in proportion to the discount and the amount raised [S8]. A placement large enough to repair the balance sheet would be material for minorities [S3].

Credit cost on the finance book is the risk the draft did not quantify. Provisions are assessed individually and collectively under the expected-credit-loss model, and receivables are written off once overdue more than six months, so a rise in consumer delinquencies hits the profit centre that carries the group [S5]. The related-party receivable of IDR3,220.2bn is a second credit exposure, this one to affiliates, and an impairment of it would fall directly on parent equity [S3].

The base case is a wide discount that persists: the parts are worth the pre-revaluation book, the cash flow stays negative through the middle of the forecast, and the discount does not narrow without a catalyst [S3][S5]. The upside case requires a corporate event: a disposal of industrial or property assets at appraised value, a term extension of the short book, a dividend upstream from the listed subsidiary, or a transaction that simplifies the group [S8][S3]. Even the bull case applies the same discount channel in the same amount as the bear, so no scenario in our set reaches the current price [S8].

Other risks are specific to this structure. The rupiah matters twice, through imported-unit costs and through foreign-currency debt, and the group discloses derivative liabilities that have moved against it [S3]. Related-party purchases at a fifth of cost of revenue mean transfer pricing is a live risk to minority economics [S3]. The controlling shareholder other interests, including the Singapore-listed holding company, create the possibility of transactions that are fair to the group but not to the minority [S8].

The equity sensitivity to the funding rate is the risk we think the market underweights. A move in the short-term rate of a single percentage point, applied to the short book the group now carries, changes the interest bill by more than the parent entire profit, so the operating earnings are not a stable anchor [S3][S5]. That is why the target is a value for the parts with an explicit discount rather than a forecast of the share price in an orderly market [S8].

Signposts that would change our view: a term extension of the short-term book beyond a year; a disposal of industrial or property assets at a price close to appraised value; a dividend upstream from the listed subsidiary; a discounted equity raise, which we would treat as dilutive; and a sustained recovery in gross margin with positive operating cash flow [S3][S5][S8].

Control is concentrated. Gallant Venture holds 49.5% of the shares, the Thohir family securities house holds a further block, and a second strategic holder accounts for most of the rest, leaving a free float that the IDX registry puts at 7.3% [S8][S0]. At that float the price is set by a marginal holder, and the controlling shareholder can influence the register, the dividend and the related-party terms without needing minority consent for ordinary resolutions [S8].

Related-party dealings are large and recurring. Purchases of goods from related parties were IDR4,902.6bn in the nine months to September 2026, about a fifth of cost of revenue, sales to related parties were a small share of revenue, and other receivables from related parties stood at IDR3,220.2bn [S3]. The latter is a claim on affiliated companies rather than on customers, and it is the clearest single channel through which value can leave the listed group [S3].

The audit is clean but the accounting carries quality flags. The FY2025 accounts were audited without modification [S5]. Inside equity, the fixed-asset revaluation surplus is IDR6,847.1bn and the investment-property fair-value gain the group took through profit or loss is IDR3,240.0bn, so the book value is a mark rather than a cost [S5][S3]. Minority dividends of a large multiple of the parent dividend show where the cash goes: the partly owned finance subsidiaries distribute to their outside shareholders while the wholly owned distribution arm absorbs the losses [S5][S8].

On ESG the material exposures are the electrification transition and the group own fleet and workshop emissions, which are modest relative to the franchise risk, and the social exposure of consumer-finance lending into a highly indebted household sector [S7][S3]. Governance is the dominant factor: a thin float, a controlling shareholder with related interests, large related-party flows and a revaluation-heavy equity base are the combination that the house card treats as a discount to fair value [S8].

The dated catalysts are the full-year wholesale number and the group December volume report, the FY2026 audited accounts and any refinancing disclosure, and the annual general meeting at which the parent dividend is declared [S6][S3][S8]. We expect the audited accounts to be the more informative event, because they will show whether the operating cash outflow of the first nine months reversed, whether the short-term book was term-extended, and whether the auditor attached any emphasis of matter [S3].

Between updates we monitor four things. First, the quarterly interim accounts for operating cash flow and short-term loans, because those two lines determine whether the funding structure is stable [S3]. Second, the gross margin and the mix between vehicle sales and after-sales, because margin is the only lever the group controls [S3][S5]. Third, Gaikindo wholesales and the battery-electric share, because a market that grows while the incumbents share falls does not help this distributor [S6][S7]. Fourth, any related-party transaction or corporate action, because at this float the controlling shareholder can change the equity story without a market test [S8].

We would revisit the rating on a capital-structure or corporate event, not on a monthly sales beat. A disposal of industrial or property assets at appraised value, applied to debt reduction, would move the equity value more than a year of volume growth, and a discounted equity raise would repair the balance sheet at the cost of dilution [S5][S8]. Until one of those happens, the equity is priced at its pre-revaluation assets and fragile on cash flow at the same time [S3][S5].

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for IMAS.JK

S8.title: IDN Financials: Indomobil pays dividends, Salim and Boy Thohir groups

S9.title: Indomobil owns 99.9% of Nissan Motor Indonesia

bear.narrative: A governance and funding discount: the multi-finance book stops growing, the group cannot roll 36,146.9bn of one-year financial liabilities at a 5% rate, a discounted equity raise to the controller dilutes minorities, and the pre-revaluation book itself is impaired as the distribution and assembly businesses keep burning cash. We widen the holdco discount to 55% — the tail of the house band — because the base mark is already the pre-revaluation book, so the only remaining asset support is the operating value of businesses that lost money in FY2025 [S3][S5].

bull.narrative: The discount narrows: a disposal of industrial or property assets at the appraised revaluation value, a term extension of the short book, or a dividend upstream from the listed multi-finance subsidiary gives the minority a dated catalyst, and the holdco discount compresses to 25% [S9][S6]. This is the only channel the scenario layer has into a book mark, so it is the mirror of the bear and is applied in the same amount.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the nine-month rate forward: revenue reached 27,492.6bn in the nine months to September 2026 against 22,720.8bn a year earlier, so the fourth quarter is grown at the same rate rather than assuming a deceleration with no evidence for it [S3]. From FY2027E growth fades toward the national market because Gaikindo wholesales reached 679,020 units in the same nine months and the industry targets 850,000 for the year, while battery-electric entrants take share [S6][S7].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The nine months to September 2026 earned an 18.5% gross margin on 27,492.6bn of revenue, down from 20.1% in the same period a year earlier as vehicle discounting and a stronger yen cost of imported units bit [S3]. FY2026E carries that nine-month rate; the path back to the 20.4% audited FY2025A level by FY2030E assumes the spare-parts and workshop mix recovers as the fleet ages and the discounting cycle passes [S5][S10]. We do not hold a permanent margin haircut below the last audited year: the compression is cyclical and sourced, not structural.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the nine months to September 2026, which is clean of bargain-purchase gains: selling expenses of 1,591.0bn plus G&A of 1,646.3bn, less other operating income of 443.2bn and plus other operating expenses of 228.7bn, on revenue of 27,492.6bn is 11.0% [S3]. The FY2025 ratio of 11.1% is NOT used as the anchor because its 1,285.6bn of other operating income includes 413.9bn of one-off bargain-purchase gains (INA 389.165, RMM 2.053, ISJ 22.647) that do not recur [S5]. Carrying 11.0% therefore embeds no non-recurring income.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 depreciation and amortisation totalled 1,351.4bn on revenue of 30,505.5bn, or 4.4%, and the FY2024 total was 1,304.1bn; the Yahoo data pack carries only about a third of this, so the fact is restated from the note [S5]. We hold the ratio flat because the asset base is workshops and rental fleet, not a depreciating concession.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Cash capital expenditure was 2,890.2bn in FY2025 and 1,964.9bn in FY2024, or 9.5% and 6.7% of revenue; the FY2025 step-up funded the vehicle-rental fleet and the INA/Nissan assembly preparation [S5][S9]. FY2026E carries the FY2025 rate; the line then converges toward a steady state of D&A at 4.43% of revenue plus growth capex as the expansion spend rolls off, reaching 5.0% in the terminal year [S5]. Holding 8.5% in perpetuity grew the asset base twice as fast as revenue and was not a defensible long-run path.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Operating working capital of 16,226.9bn against FY2025 revenue of 30,505.5bn is 53.2%, and we hold that level [S5]. It is NOT consumer-financing receivables alone: the multi-finance book is only 7,290.8bn net at December 2025 [S5]; the ratio is total trade and financing receivables, inventories and customer advances less payables, which is why 53.2% is the right description. FY2025A showed a 1,115.5bn working-capital release, but that was a one-year unwind of inventory and advances, not a new incremental ratio: holding the level at the last audited year is the anchor, and a growing finance book consumes cash with revenue growth.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Taxed at the 22% statutory rate the LK discloses, not at the 61.8% levered effective rate: the engine applies the rate to EBIT (an unlevered base), and the excess over 22% in FY2025 is a parent-level 339.7bn of non-deductible "Lain-lain" plus final-taxed dividend and rent income of 241.0bn and 32.4bn, items that do not scale with consolidated EBIT [S5 note 18c]. Taxing EBIT at 22% is the only defensible treatment; the permanent differences are disclosed in §3 rather than loaded into a rate that would also tax operating profit twice.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Finance charges of 2,033.8bn in the nine months to September 2026 annualise to 2,711.7bn against average gross debt near 54.5tn, a 5.0% rate, down from the 6.0% the three-year history implies as Bank Indonesia cut [S3][S5]. The group re-prices short-term working-capital loans quarterly, so the current rate, not the historical average, is the right forward input.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Finance income of 299.9bn in FY2025 against opening cash of 3,174.5bn is a 9.4% yield, but a large part is interest charged to related-party receivables rather than to deposits [S5][S3]. We use 5.5% on the deposit balance, close to the JIBOR-linked rate the treasury actually earns.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Gross debt rose from 51,288.0bn at December 2025 to 57,689.8bn at September 2026, with 15,266.6bn of short-term loans outstanding, because the operating cash outflow of 4,967.1bn was funded with borrowings [S3]. Nine months of 2026 already added 6,401.8bn of gross debt and pushed net debt to 54,531.2bn, so FY2026E must carry at least that and a fourth quarter funded the same way: we set 12,000bn, which funds the nine-month outflow and a similar fourth quarter rather than assuming the gap closes [S3]. The engine builds cash as the balancing item, so the forecast net-debt line is still driven by FCFF and remains below the September actual; section 3 discloses the gap and the scenario build does not depend on it. The line then declines as revenue growth slows: 8,000, 5,000, 3,000 and 2,000bn.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2025 equity in net earnings of associates was 73.3bn and final income tax was 34.4bn, both reported below the operating line, leaving 38.9bn of net other items [S5]. We hold that run-rate flat rather than extrapolating the 211.3bn of associate earnings booked in FY2024, which included one-off gains at the joint ventures.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests took 100.1bn of the 232.4bn FY2025 net profit, or 43.1%, because the profitable multi-finance and rental subsidiaries carry large outside stakes while the wholly-owned distribution arm lost money [S5][S3]. The three-year average of 32% understates the current share, so we use 42%.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend was 15.98bn, or Rp4 a share, a 12.1% payout of the 132.3bn parent profit, while minorities took a further 145.7bn [S5][S8]. With a 4,967.1bn operating cash outflow in the nine months to September 2026, 36,146.9bn of financial liabilities maturing within a year and only 3,158.6bn of cash, we assume the parent dividend is suspended through the forecast rather than funded with new debt [S3].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Issued shares have been 3,994,291,039 since the 2019 rights issue and no new mandate is disclosed in the FY2025 accounts [S5]. A discounted placement to the controlling shareholder is carried as a bear-case dilution risk in §5, not in the base share count, because no share issuance has been announced [S5][S8].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Terminal growth of 4% is below long-run Indonesian nominal GDP and below the 5% the house card allows for a compounder; it is retained for the FCFF cross-check arithmetic even though the target is built on the parts, because the SOTP carries the asset marks and the DCF only frames the cash throw [S5].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Held at 40%, the wide end of the 20-40% house band, and argued rather than asserted. The governance file justifies the wide end: Gallant Venture holds 49.49% and the free float is 7.34%, related-party purchases are 4,902.6bn or 22% of cost of revenue, and other receivables from related parties are 3,220.2bn [S8][S3]. The name own history supports the wide end rather than the midpoint: its reported P/B has run 0.27x (FY2024A), 0.42x (FY2023A), 0.29x (FY2022A) and 0.34x (FY2025A), and the 52-week range of the price (high and low in the data pack) brackets 0.40x to 0.21x of book, so the market has never paid anything close to the parts and there is no 5-year episode of a narrow discount to point to [S0]. The house base rate for discount narrowing (data/base_rates.yaml holdco_discount_narrowing) completes only 33% of the time over three years with a +28%/-18% spread, so the discount is not assumed to narrow; it is the base rate and governance is its DNA. The scenario tails run to 55% (bear) and 25% (bull) because the discount is the only channel the scenario layer has into a balance-sheet mark.

challenges.challenge: The 45% tax rate is a levered effective rate applied to an unlevered base. The engine taxes EBIT (fcff = ebit*(1 - a.tax_rate) + da - capex - delta_nwc), but the basis cites 341.3 + 34.4 on 608.2 of post-interest pre-tax profit = 61.8%. Note 18c (S5 p.168) shows the statutory rate is 22% and the excess is the parent's 339.7bn non-deductible "Lain-lain" plus final-taxed dividends 241.0bn and rent 32.4bn. At 22% FY2026E FCFF excluding the working-capital charge is +268bn, not negative; at 45% it is -355bn. So §4's claim that "even if we removed the financing book from working capital entirely, the capex and tax lines alone would keep free cash flow negative" is true only at the 45% rate.
challenges.answer: Taxed EBIT at the 22% statutory rate disclosed in note 18c and itemised the parent-level permanent differences (339.7bn non-deductible Lain-lain, 241.0bn final-taxed dividends, 32.4bn rent) in section 3 instead of loading them into a rate applied to EBIT. Re-ran the engine: FCFF is still negative through the middle of the forecast at 22%, so the claim that capex and tax alone keep it negative was removed and the DCF is now a disclosed cross-check, not a weighted method.

challenges.challenge: The only method that produces the target is P/E of 414 = 12.51 x 132.335bn, described as "last-twelve-month parent earnings". 132.335 is FY2025A (F14); true LTM parent earnings are -110.1bn (9M2026 15.184 F26 plus Q4-2025 132.335 - 257.597 = -125.262). The FY2025A base is also inflated by the "Others" segment's 1,892.8bn net income on 675.8bn of revenue (S5 p.263), which fell to 141.7bn in 9M2026 (S3 p.173), and by ~414bn of bargain-purchase gains inside other operating income. A method whose base is negative on the stated period cannot produce Rp414.
challenges.answer: Removed the P/E method entirely. True LTM parent earnings are negative (9M2026 15.184bn plus Q4-2025 of -125.262bn), and the FY2025A base is inflated by the Others segment and the bargain-purchase gains, so no multiple can be applied. Section 4 states the base, the period and why the method is unavailable; the target is built on the parts.

challenges.challenge: No sum-of-parts for a holding company. fund record has no holdings block and no holdco_net_debt, yet IMAS owns 91.97% of listed PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk (S5 p.27; S8), a 27.1tn-asset "Others" segment, 4.20tn of investments in shares (S5 p.263) and a 6.85tn revaluation surplus; the equity trades at 0.22x parent book (multiples.FY2025A.pbv). MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE requires holding companies to be valued on their parts; the report explicitly refuses a P/B cross-check instead.
challenges.answer: Built the SOTP: 91.97% of listed IMJS at market (1,347.0bn) plus non-IMJ distribution, assembly, industrial and property at parent book equity net of the IMJ stake (8,767.5bn), no double-counted net debt, a 40% holdco discount and the house liquidity ladder. The pre-revaluation floor is disclosed as the downside asset mark.

challenges.challenge: The weighted blend of floored methods is not a triangulation: DCF (50%) and EV/EBITDA (20%) both return exactly zero, so the 124.3078 blend is just 30% x 414.36. Worse, the scenario framework is inert: base, bear and bull all return v0 124.30778 and tp 150.71542 (fund record), because the shocks move revenue_growth and gross_margin while the only live method reads FY2025A actual earnings. A 45/30/25 probability weighting over three identical outcomes carries no information.
challenges.answer: Weights are now SOTP 1.0; the floored DCF and EV/EBITDA are no longer weighted. Scenarios are mirrored on the only live channel, the holdco discount (+/-15pp), and now produce distinct outputs: bear 1,139.51, base 1,519.35, bull 1,899.19 per share.

challenges.challenge: The "Others" segment earns 1,892.8bn of net income on 675.8bn of revenue in FY2025 (gross profit 978.3bn, 145% margin, S5 p.263) and holds 27.1tn of assets, and the report describes it only as "a residual group of industrial, property and service businesses". It is the largest single contributor to consolidated profit and the base of the only live valuation method, and it collapses to 141.7bn in 9M2026. The reader cannot tell whether consolidated earnings power is better or worse than modelled.
challenges.answer: The Others segment is now described and quantified (1,892.8bn FY2025 net income, F44), identified as partly non-recurring bargain-purchase gains, stripped from the earnings base and carried at book equity inside the SOTP rather than capitalised as a recurring stream.

challenges.challenge: BEV is framed only as a threat, but the group is itself a BEV and assembly participant: PT Aion Indomobil Distribution Indonesia (51%) and PT Indomobil Zeeda Energi (100%) (S5 p.27), and INA (ex-NMI) at 99.81% acquired for Rp578bn with a 389.2bn bargain-purchase gain (S5 p.45). Neither the assembly earnings stream nor the BEV distribution channel is assigned any value, and the 15.9% BEV share (F40) is treated as entirely lost to the group.
challenges.answer: Section 1 now names the BEV and assembly positions (Aion majority, Zeeda wholly owned, INA at the acquired stake) and states that their earnings and assets sit inside the consolidated book equity that the SOTP values, so they are not assigned zero; no separate growth value is added and the reason is given.

challenges.challenge: A rights issue is presented as one of three things that "would change our mind" in a favourable direction (summary, §5). At 0.22x book, 49.49% control and a float under 14%, a discounted rights issue or placement to the controller is the most likely recapitalisation route and is materially dilutive to minorities — a downside, not a remedy. No dilution is modelled in the bear case, and the free-float position against the IDX minimum is not checked.
challenges.answer: Recast a discounted raise as a downside: section 5 now treats a placement or rights issue to the controller as the likeliest recapitalisation and the dilution channel for minorities, and the bear case widens the discount rather than presenting a raise as a remedy. Float is taken from the IDX registry figure.

challenges.challenge: There is no provisioning or credit-cost analysis of the finance book, which is the profit centre the report says carries the group. The report instead applies the Sloan accruals ratio ("the accruals ratio is adverse"), which EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS §1 says is meaningless on a financial balance sheet and must be replaced by provisioning-versus-write-off trends. Related-party other receivables of 3,220.2bn (F33, S3 p.153) are a claim on affiliates, and no impairment sensitivity is run.
challenges.answer: Removed the Sloan accruals test as invalid for a multifinance balance sheet and replaced it with the provisioning and write-off policy (ECL, six-month write-off) and the related-party receivable exposure of 3,220.2bn to parent equity; credit cost is carried as a bear-case risk.

challenges.challenge: Unjustified optimism: opex_pct 11.1% is derived as (gross profit - operating income)/revenue, so it nets FY2025 other operating income of 1,285.6bn (S5 p.18) which includes about 414bn of one-off bargain-purchase gains (INA 389.165, RMM 2.053, other 22.647; S5 pp.45-49). Carrying 11.1% flat for ten years embeds ~414bn/yr of non-recurring gains, overstating EBIT by roughly 15% in every forecast year.
challenges.answer: Recalibrated opex to 11.0% on the clean 9M2026 figures, which exclude the 413.9bn of bargain-purchase gains inside FY2025 other operating income, so the forecast embeds no non-recurring income. The basis states the arithmetic and the excluded items.

challenges.challenge: Stacked unjustified conservatism that shapes the negative FCFF: (1) terminal gross margin 19.5% never returns to the FY2025A actual 20.4%, with no source; (2) the calibration gate reports a -1.85pp EBITDA-margin gap versus FY2025A and no qc_justification answers it; (3) capex 8.5% of revenue against D&A 4.43% in perpetuity with 4% terminal growth, an internally inconsistent asset-intensity path; (4) nwc_pct 54% held flat although FY2025A delta_nwc was a -1,115bn release (cov_engine explain).
challenges.answer: Gross margin now reverts to the FY2025A actual of 20.4% by FY2030E, capex converges to 5.0% (D&A 4.43% plus growth), the working-capital basis is corrected to total operating working capital, and the calibration gap is answered in qc_justifications with sources.

challenges.challenge: The DCF applies a Gordon-growth terminal value to a negative FY2035E FCFF of -899.2bn (TV about -11.7tn, roughly 30% of the -12,740bn EV). A perpetuity of negative cash flow is not an admissible terminal treatment for a going concern, and the report quotes the -12,740bn figure as evidence of the finding.
challenges.answer: The DCF is no longer weighted and section 4 states that a negative perpetuity is not an admissible terminal treatment; the value is carried by the SOTP and the DCF is shown only as a cash-throw cross-check that floors at zero.

challenges.challenge: The free-float figure does not reconcile with its source. The report says 7.3% [S0][S8] and builds the 20% liquidity discount and the marginal-price argument on it; S8 lists Gallant 49.49%, TRIM 13.97%, Tritunggal Intipermata 18.17%, Sejahtera Raya Perkasa 6.27% and three sub-5% holders totalling 93.65%, then says "the public holds a total of 13.97%", which sums to 107.6%. The residual implied is 6.35%, close to but not the same as 7.3%, and the 20% liquidity discount has no source.
challenges.answer: Free float is taken from the IDX registry (7.34%) and the internal inconsistency of the secondary register is disclosed rather than used; the 20% liquidity discount is identified as the house ladder for a stock below the turnover threshold, not a sourced company input.

missing_bull_case.note: The 1,892.8bn FY2025 net income of the "Others" segment (on only 675.8bn of revenue, S5 p.263) is 70% of consolidated profit and appears nowhere in the report or the valuation. It collapsed to 141.7bn in 9M2026 (S3 p.173), so it is probably one-off, but the report settles neither way: if recurring the thesis is too bearish, if one-off the P/E base is inflated. Separately, the group is itself a BEV and assembly participant — Aion Indomobil Distribution (51%), Indomobil Zeeda Energi (100%) and INA (ex-NMI) at 99.81% for Rp578bn (S5 pp.27, 45) — all valued at zero while BEV is treated only as a threat.

missing_bear_case.note: A discounted rights issue or placement is listed as an upside remedy ("a rights issue that repairs the equity", summary and §5) when at 0.22x book, with 49.49% control and a float under 14%, a discounted raise to the controller is the standard dilution channel and is a downside for minorities. The bear case also has no provisioning or credit-cost analysis on the finance book, and uses the Sloan accruals ratio which EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS says is meaningless on a multifinance balance sheet (use provisioning vs write-off trends instead).

assumption_realism.note: tax_rate 45% is applied by the engine to EBIT (fcff = ebit*(1-tax)+da-capex-delta_nwc, cov_engine explain) but is calibrated on post-interest pre-tax profit (341.3bn + 34.4bn on 608.2bn = 61.8%). Note 18c shows the statutory rate is 22% and the excess comes from the parent's 339.7bn of non-deductible "Lain-lain" plus final-taxed income (dividends 241.0bn, rent 32.4bn) — items that do not scale with EBIT. Also nwc_pct 54% is stated as "consumer-financing receivables" of 20.3tn, but the LK shows financing receivables of only 7,818.7bn (S3 p.4); 0.54 is total receivables/revenue, so the basis misdescribes the driver.

evidence_and_citations.note: Six spot-checks verify verbatim: operating outflow 9M2026 -4,967,066 (F27, S3 p.10), financial liabilities due within one year 36,146,945 (F30, S3 p.5), revaluation surplus 6,847,108 (F34, S5), automotive segment net loss -4,075,855 (F36, S5 p.263), parent stake 49.49% (F37, S8), dividends to parent 15,977 (F20, S5). The D&A/EBIT/dividends restatements are correctly sourced. The free-float citation does not reconcile: the report says 7.3% [S0][S8] but S8 lists Gallant 49.49%, TRIM 13.97%, Tritunggal 18.17%, Sejahtera 6.27% and three sub-5% holders, summing to 93.65% before the "public" line, which it calls 13.97% (a total of 107.6%).

valuation_method_fit.note: The house method card requires holding companies to be valued on their parts (holdings with market|house|multiple|book, plus holdco_net_debt); fund record has no holdings block and no SOTP, although the report itself calls IMAS a holding company and it owns 91.97% of listed PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk (S5 p.27; S8), a 27.1tn-asset "Others" segment and 4.20tn of investments in shares. The consolidated DCF and EV/EBITDA both floor to zero and 70% of the blend weight is therefore inert; the target is just 30% x the P/E. The negative terminal value on a negative FCFF is not an admissible Gordon-growth treatment, though it does not change the floored outcome.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says more than the evidence in two places: the P/E base of 132.3bn is called "last-twelve-month" when it is FY2025A and true LTM parent earnings are -110.1bn (9M2026 15.184 less Q4-2025 -125.262); and "interest cover near one time" is gross (2,820.5/2,585.5 = 1.09x) when net interest cover is 1.23x and EBITDA cover 1.61x. Conversely the report is candid that the DCF floor is the finding and that the asset base is real — credit for that. The two errors point in opposite directions (P/E base too high, DCF too negative) and the net is never reconciled.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The WACC of 12.0% sits near the peers (AUTO.JK 11.86%, DRMA.JK 11.87%) and the 50/30/20 weights match the AUTOS_COMPONENTS card, but the COE of 21.2% is far above the peer 12.0% (AUTO.JK, BOGA.JK, DRMA.JK) because beta is relevered to 2.30 at "market gearing 2.00x"; the market D/E implied by 51.9tn of net debt against a 2.98tn market cap is ~17x, so the 2.00x input is unsourced and drives a COE that then lifts the target by 21% in the roll-forward. Macro deck variables (usd_idr 18,350, bi_rate 5.75) are read, and the rupiah exposure is discussed.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative side, unsourced: terminal gross margin 19.5% never returns to the FY2025A actual of 20.4%, leaving a permanent 0.9pp of margin; the 1.85pp calibration gap (actual 13.68% vs model 11.83% EBITDA margin) is not answered in qc_justifications; capex 8.5% of revenue against D&A 4.43% in perpetuity with 4% terminal growth grows the asset base twice as fast as revenue forever; and nwc_pct 54% is held flat although the last actual FY2025A was a 1,115bn working-capital release (cov_engine explain delta_nwc). Optimistic side, unsourced: opex_pct 11.1% nets 1,285.6bn of other operating income that includes about 414bn of one-off bargain-purchase gains (INA 389.2, RMM 2.1, other 22.6; S5 pp.45-49), overstating EBIT by ~15% for ten years.

calibration.note: qc shows no blocking flag and both BLOCKs are justified with sources that say what is claimed; the balance-sheet bridge to the September net debt (+51,895.3 pack net debt, -2,635.9 post-balance-sheet increase = 54,531.2, matching 57,689.8 gross debt less 3,158.6 cash) is correct and unusually well documented. The calibration gate nevertheless reports a -1.85pp EBITDA-margin gap against FY2025A with no qc_justification, and MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE requires every drift answered.

signoff.notes: SELL is not a batch template artefact: this name runs holdco_sotp, not the AUTOS_COMPONENTS consolidated DCF behind the AUTO/GJTL BUYs, so the direction difference has a method reason. The direction survives removing either discount: without the 20% liquidity leg the target is 573 (-23%), without the 21% COE roll it is 378. The two discounts are disclosed and symmetric in the scenario frame - holdco 40% sourced to governance facts (49.49% Gallant control, 7.34% IDX float, 22% related-party purchases, 3,220.2bn related-party receivables) and varied +/-15pp across base/bear/bull, while the 20% liquidity leg is house policy applied uniformly to all three scenarios. Residual, not decisive: the thin float partly justifies both legs (partial illiquidity overlap) and the -38.5% magnitude rests on house-policy discounts, but the rating carries without the liquidity leg. No SOTP double count: IMJ at market equity 1,347.0 plus non-IMJ at parent book equity net of the IMJ stake 1,839.0 gross to 3,186.0, and consolidated net debt is not deducted again because both blocks are already equity marks. All twelve FATAL/MATERIAL challenges are answered on substance; QC round-2 Q1 (F46 investment-property mark retained, optimistic) and Q2 (whole-surplus strip, conservative) offset and are disclosed. Desk flag: fund record industry reads CONGLOMERATES while the batch assigns AUTOS_COMPONENTS - reconcile the coverage-index label, and keep Q5 (fold the two discounts or state they measure distinct factors) as a note for the next revision.

bias.note: SELL is robust to the discount stack: without the 20% liquidity leg the target is 573 (-23%), and without the 21% COE roll it is 378. Direction is supported by sourced facts (IMJ stake 1,347.0 at market vs 5,019.0 book; non-IMJ pre-revaluation book 1,839.0). Optimism (F46 3,240.0 investment-property mark retained; COE roll on static book) and conservatism (whole-surplus strip; 40%+20% stacked) are offsetting, so the rating carries no directional bias, though the -38.5% magnitude rests on two house-policy discounts rather than sourced facts.

recomputed.item: IMJ stake at market (IDR bn, 0.9197 x 1,464.7)

findings.finding: The 1,839.0bn non-IMJ book still carries the 3,240.0bn investment-property fair-value gain (F46, S3) - 1.8x the book and 102% of the 3,186.0bn gross SOTP - so the ex-F46 operating book is about -1,401bn. It is disclosed in section 4, but the pre-revaluation label and the floor argument must state that the base non-IMJ value rests on that appraisal mark.

The whole 6,928.5bn surplus is stripped from parent equity after the IMJ stake was removed at book 5,019.0bn (91.97% of IMJS 5,501.1bn less 43.3bn NCI). Any part of the surplus inside IMJS is stripped twice; S5 note 25 shows one parent-attributable line with no entity split. This is the one route by which the round-1 fix could over-correct.

calibration.ebitda_margin and extreme_call are orphan justification IDs in fund record (the engine reports them unmatched), so the -1.75pp calibration gate reads unjustified mechanically even though the text is right (9M2026 gross margin 18.5% vs FY2025A 20.4%, S3).

COE 21.24% (beta 2.304 on the engine de=2.0 industry default) is applied as a 12-month roll-forward to a static book NAV, adding 21% (479 to 580). A book mark accretes at ROE (2-6%), not COE; the roll is optimistic but does not change the SELL.

The 40% holdco discount and 20% liquidity discount compound to a 52% haircut on a value already struck at pre-revaluation book. Scenarios are mirrored (+/-15pp on the same driver, base 45%) and distinct; the rating survives without the liquidity leg, but check the two discounts do not double-count control and illiquidity.

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -4.5pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Capex falls from 9.47% of revenue in FY2026E to 5.0% by FY2030E because the FY2025-26 step-up is expansion (vehicle-rental fleet, INA/Nissan assembly) that rolls off; the terminal 5.0% is D&A at 4.43% plus growth capex, the internally consistent steady state [S5][S9].

flags.message: dividends_paid FY2025A restated at 0.10x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack figure of 160.9bn is total dividends paid by the consolidated group, of which 145.7bn went to non-controlling interests; the statement of changes in equity shows 15,977m paid to parent shareholders, which is the Rp4 a share declared at the June 2026 AGMS [S5][S8]. Only the parent figure belongs in the equity roll-forward.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'sotp': 0.6, 'pe': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: SOTP is weighted at 100% because it is the only method that produces a value for a holding company whose listed stake trades at 0.27x book and whose consolidated FCFF is negative [S5][S3]; P/E on true LTM parent earnings of -110.1bn is unavailable and EV/EBITDA floors at zero, so weighting them would put 70% of the blend on methods that return zero, which the red team correctly rejected.
